medications.sig: Take 4 tablets (40 mg) by mouth every morning, then taper as directed by nephrology

documents.title: Nephrology Follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology note, visit 2/13/2023, received 2/15/2023.

About 16 weeks on prednisone 60 mg. No edema, energy back. Tolerating prednisone and losartan.

Urine protein/creatinine 0.18 g/g. Serum albumin 3.9 g/dL. Creatinine stable.

Assessment: FSGS in complete remission.

Plan: begin taper: prednisone 40 mg daily for 4 weeks, then 30 mg for 4 weeks, 20 mg for 4 weeks, then down by 5 mg every 3-4 weeks to off (written schedule given). Continue losartan 25 mg. Recheck at the end of the taper.

cc: primary care physician

documents.title: Cetirizine refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy refill request for cetirizine 10 mg #90. Last filled 4/2022. Approved per protocol, 3 refills.

documents.title: Cancellation
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt cancelled tomorrow's physical; finals week and he is proctoring. Rebooked for July 11, morning.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled physical. Kidney disease went into remission in February; now near the bottom of the prednisone taper (10 mg a day this week), still on losartan 25 mg. Feels like himself again. Back to basketball. Allergies mild this spring.

Meds: prednisone per taper, losartan 25 mg daily, cetirizine 10 mg PRN. NKDA.

Exam: well. No periorbital puffiness. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen benign. No edema. Skin: few forehead papules, unchanged.
PHQ-9 2.

A/P:
- FSGS in remission, taper nearly done; nephrology following. Glucose on today's chemistry is a reasonable check while on steroids. Urine protein today.
- Lipids deferred until he's off prednisone; nephrology rechecking at the end of the taper.
- Allergic rhinitis, acne: unchanged.
- Flu shot in the fall. See in a year.

documents.title: Nephrology Follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology note, visit 8/14/2023, received 8/16/2023.

Took his last prednisone dose last week. No edema, no foamy urine.
Urinalysis negative for protein; urine protein/creatinine under 0.2 g/g. Albumin normal. Cholesterol now in the normal range without treatment.

Assessment: FSGS, sustained complete remission, off steroids.
Plan: continue losartan for now; reassess next month. Reviewed relapse signs (swelling, foamy urine) and to call promptly.

cc: primary care physician

documents.title: Nephrology Follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology note, visit 9/18/2023, received 9/20/2023.

Seven months in remission, five weeks off prednisone. BP normal off any other agents; urine albumin normal.
Decision with patient: stop losartan and follow. Home BP check occasionally. Yearly visit with urine and chemistry, sooner with any swelling or foamy urine. 

Current meds: cetirizine 10 mg PRN.

cc: primary care physician

documents.title: Flu shot
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine given, R deltoid, 0.5 mL IM. Afebrile, feeling well. He had the 2023-24 COVID vaccine at his pharmacy on 10/6; card shown, entered in immunization record. No problems after either.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, he's at home. Runny nose, scratchy throat and cough since Friday; a lot of it going through the building. Low-grade temps, highest 100.1. No dyspnea, no chest pain, no ear or sinus pain. Home COVID test negative today. No swelling or foamy urine.

Comfortable on camera, nasal voice, no audible wheeze, talking easily.

Viral URI. Fluids, rest, acetaminophen, saline. Stay home tomorrow if febrile. Message us if fever climbs or lasts past the weekend, or anything feels off.

conditions.label: Systemic inflammatory response syndrome
conditions.note: after viral respiratory infection; cultures sent

reports.text: PA and lateral views. Lungs clear. No consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Mediastinum unremarkable.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, visit 4/1/2024, received 4/2/2024.

38-year-old man, history of FSGS in remission off treatment, presenting with fever and generally feeling unwell. Cold symptoms for about 10 days, seen by video by his PCP last week; today worse, with chills, aches and fatigue. Mild cough. No dyspnea, chest pain, dysuria, abdominal pain, headache or neck stiffness. No rash.
Meds: cetirizine PRN. NKDA. Never smoker.

Triage: T 38.7, HR 112, BP 124/74, RR 20, SpO2 97% RA.
Exam: ill-appearing but nontoxic. Oropharynx mildly erythematous. Neck supple. Lungs clear. Heart tachycardic, regular. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Skin without rash.

Results: WBC 13.6. CRP 87 mg/L. Chemistry with normal creatinine. UA no protein, no infection. CXR clear. Blood cultures x2 sent.

Course: 2 L IV fluids, acetaminophen 1 g. Repeat T 37.4, HR 88, feeling much better, tolerating PO.

Impression: systemic inflammatory response following a viral upper respiratory infection; no bacterial source identified.
Disposition: home. PCP follow-up in 2-3 days; we will call with any positive culture. Return for persistent fever, breathing trouble, confusion or new swelling.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in the ED Monday night for fever and malaise after his cold; inflammatory markers up (WBC 13.6, CRP 87), fluids and acetaminophen, home same night. Cultures pending at discharge, nothing called back so far.

Since then: no fever after Tuesday morning, cough nearly gone, back at work today. No swelling.

Exam: afebrile, HR in the 70s. Throat clear, lungs clear, heart regular. No edema.

A/P: SIRS after a viral URI, resolved clinically. CBC and CRP today to document recovery; will chase final blood cultures. URI resolved. FSGS in remission: ED urine had no protein, reassuring.

documents.title: ED blood culture result
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Addendum from the regional hospital ED: blood cultures from 4/1 final, no growth at 5 days. Scanned and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Follow-up labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Andre, Thursday's blood count and CRP are back to normal, and the ED's blood cultures grew nothing. That episode is behind you. Glad you're feeling well.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam. School's out. No illness since the April ED trip. No swelling, urine looks normal. Allergy season was manageable. Plays basketball twice a week.

Meds: cetirizine 10 mg as needed. NKDA. Never smoker, weekend drinks.

Exam: well. ENT normal. Neck supple. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Extremities without edema. Skin with mild comedonal acne on forehead.
PHQ-2 negative.

Plan:
- Preventive: labs (CMP, CBC, lipids, UA). Vaccines: flu in the fall; COVID per season.
- FSGS, remission since 2/2023, off all treatment; nephrology yearly in September.
- SIRS 4/2024: resolved.
- Rhinitis and acne unchanged.
RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Nephrology Annual Visit
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology note, visit 9/16/2024, received 9/18/2024.

FSGS, complete remission since 2/2023, off immunosuppression and RAAS blockade for a year. ED visit in April for a febrile inflammatory response after a viral illness, recovered; urine stayed protein-free.
Today BP normal, no edema. Urine negative for protein, urine albumin normal, creatinine stable.
Plan: continue observation; yearly visit. Call for edema or foamy urine.

cc: primary care physician

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM to left arm. Screening questions negative. He reports this year's COVID shot at a pharmacy 10/3; added to record. Tolerated without issue.
